1.explanation: We create a minimal web server that serves a large JSON response under /api/blob with gzip compression enabled via the express-compression middleware. We then use Puppeteer to launch Chrome (so Lighthouse will connect) and invoke the Lighthouse module programmatically against http://localhost:3000.  Finally, we print out the “Enable text compression” audit details.  Under Chrome 63 dev, you will see the same bug: Lighthouse flags your gzipped /api/blob endpoint as uncompressed.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse on a page that serves a large JSON endpoint (/api/blob) with Content-Encoding: gzip, the “Enable text compression” audit still lists /api/blob as uncompressed.  In the screenshot you see multiple rows of "/api/blob" each ~29–30 KB original and ~23 KB savings, even though a curl -I shows Content-Encoding: gzip and Chrome’s Network panel shows the response is gzipped.
